A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WiLoR and provide readable text, equations, figures and tables. The supplied v1 ends with references; v2 adds supplementary Sections 7–11. The retained material can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original hand-detection, 3D reconstruction, ablation and temporal-coherence results in Tables 1–6 and qualitative figures.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments, revises detection results and adds qualitative failure examples in supplementary Figure 7.

M1.justification: The DarkNet/PANet detector, ViT token regressor, multi-scale mesh refinement and training objectives are retained. V2 clarifies pose representation and supplies implementation details; these disclosures do not establish a changed computational procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 14 reconstruction-training datasets and the same detection, reconstruction and temporal-evaluation benchmarks. Supplementary Section 10 expands descriptions of existing training data. Table 7 compares dataset characteristics without establishing additional training or evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–6 and the qualitative reconstruction comparison is unchanged. ViTDet remains the same named comparator despite revised scores; additional citations and the dataset-comparison table do not introduce evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: Section 3 revises the stated WHIM source-video count from more than 1,500 to more than 1,400. This changes the reported collection size without establishing an actual corpus reduction or rerun. Existing evaluation metrics remain unchanged; supplementary training settings are newly disclosed.

E4.justification: V2 adds Figure 7, showing reconstruction failures on complex finger poses and missed small hands in crowded scenes. This adds a concrete failure-case analysis. The existing component, backbone, training-data and augmentation ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests for the experiments. The added implementation details do not introduce uncertainty-estimation practices.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially revises ViTDet’s AP0.5/mAP: COCO-Whole changes from 17.17/3.16 to 41.64/13.21, Oxford-Hands from 7.49/1.44 to 67.56/29.77, and WHIM from 38.81/8.12 to 84.76/35.42. These changes materially alter its ranking and reported gaps to WiLoR. WiLoR’s scores and Tables 2–6 remain unchanged; Figure 7 adds qualitative failure results.

T1.justification: Section 3 corrects the weighted-box expression in Equation 1 from weighting yi to weighting bi, and changes the PCA basis dimensions from 3N by d to d by 3N, matching the matrix products. Section 4.2 also changes the stated MANO pose dimension from 45 to 48. These are limited formal corrections; no new theoretical results or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same full-stack reconstruction, WHIM dataset, accuracy and temporal-coherence claims. The conclusion revises the detector-speed claim from over 110 FPS to over 130 FPS, consistent with the already reported 138 FPS result.

C2.justification: New Section 9 substantially qualifies applicability: training remains concentrated on common poses, extreme articulations and crowded scenes cause failures, independent hand reconstruction can miss contacts, and camera-space predictions do not establish accurate world-space reconstruction. It explains these limitations and proposes targeted remedies, whereas v1 lacks this discussion.

D1.justification: New Section 7 supplies previously absent optimizers, learning-rate schedules, epoch budgets, loss weights, detector batch size, hardware and training duration. It also specifies token initialization, rotation representation, feature-map dimensions and upsampling details. Section 10 adds dataset sizes, annotation types and BEDLAM cropping information. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation without establishing that existing experiments were reconfigured.

R1.justification: V2 adds eight references, including spiral convolutional networks, Panoptic Studio, MS-MANO, Metric3D and HaWoR. Table 7 adds explicit positioning against existing hand datasets. These extend architectural context and discussion of limitations while retaining the original research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 makes distributed grammar and terminology corrections, completes unfinished prose and slightly revises subsection headings. It adds an organized supplement, but the main paper’s section sequence and argument remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the dataset-comparison Table 7 and failure-case Figure 7. Existing figures are retained with resizing and page reflow; Tables 1–2 gain metric-direction arrows, and Table 6 loses its unsupported caption statement about including ground-truth values. The overall visual organization remains similar.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the added training specifications, formal corrections and concrete failure analysis make v2 easier to reproduce and assess. These gains are tempered by unexplained large ViTDet score revisions and the new blanket 100-fold dataset-size claim, which Table 7 does not support for every listed comparator. The net improvement is principally in documentation and qualification of the retained work.
